panels.rationale: Caption explicitly attributes excoriations, scratch marks, and prurigo nodules to ICP; in-text describes these as secondary lesions from scratching in ICP. Image shows multiple excoriated papules/nodules on back/buttocks consistent with that.

in_text_mentions: zed by severe pruritus with no primary skin lesions with or without jaundice, which is seen in 0.02–2.4% [23]. Pruritus typically starts on the palms and soles and later becomes generalized. Later secondary lesions such as excoriations, scratch marks, and prurigo nodules might develop as a result of scratching (Figure 4). This commonly involves the shins and lower arms. The symptoms usually disappear 1-2 days after delivery, but in some cases they can persist for 1-2 weeks [9]. There is a high risk of recurrence of ICP in subsequent pregnancies (50–70%) and with the use of oral contraceptives.
